title: The 3-Second Rule
tagline: You have roughly 3 seconds to earn a prospect's curiosity before an outbound message gets ignored, and spending those seconds pitching loses it.
excerpt: You have roughly 3 seconds to earn a prospect's curiosity before an outbound message gets ignored, and pitching in that window loses it.
definition: you have exactly 3 seconds to earn a prospect's interest in a cold outbound message. If those seconds are spent pitching features, listing service offerings, or introducing company history, the prospect has already moved on. The message's sole job in that window is to earn curiosity, not to explain the product.

steps.text: The opening line's only job is to make someone want to read the next one.
A generic feature-dump opener signals a salesperson looking to take up time, and gets the same treatment as spam.
A sharp, specific observation about the prospect's situation disarms the usual filtering reflex a busy inbox trains people to have.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: Decision-makers skim their inboxes like skeptics, not fans. Outbound isn't dead as a channel, but treating every touch like a generic broadcast instead of a high-leverage, individual moment is what keeps reply rates stuck at zero.
